steps.headline: The arrowhead picker falls off the screen
steps.narration: When you select an arrow and click one of the arrowhead buttons in the properties panel, a small popup appears to pick the arrowhead style. The bug is that this popup can overflow the visible area and be partially or fully hidden off the edge of the screen. On phones the problem is most visible.

steps.say: On phones the popup was placed to the right of the trigger button, but the arrowhead panel itself sits near the right side of the screen, so the popup had nowhere to go.

lines.annotation: `formFactor === "phone"` means screen width ≤ ~599 px — exactly where overflow is most likely.
On a phone, this sends the popup rightward into the viewport edge.

beats.text: The `isMobile` flag drove the `side` and `sideOffset` props of the Radix popover. On a phone it moved the popup to the right instead of below.
beats.heading: How it worked before

beats.text: The properties panel is already at the right side of the screen. Sending the popup further right pushes it outside the editor container.

steps.title: On phones, the picker was sent to the right — near the screen edge
steps.headline: Phone layout sent picker towards the screen edge
steps.narration: The picker component checked whether the device was a phone and, if so, opened the popup to the right of the trigger button. The arrowhead panel sits in the properties sidebar near the right edge of the screen. Opening to the right from that position puts the popup beyond the viewport.

steps.say: The floating panel library already had instructions to keep the popup inside the editor container, but a competing CSS rule was moving it independently, so the guard had no effect.

lines.annotation: This already restricts placement to the editor div — but the absolutely-positioned inner div undermines it.

beats.text: `collisionBoundary={container ?? undefined}` tells Radix to keep the popup inside the Excalidraw host div. That prop was already present before this PR.
beats.heading: The guard in place

lines.annotation: An absolutely-positioned child can move independently from where Radix placed the parent portal.

beats.text: The inner wrapper div had absolute positioning set in the stylesheet. This lets it escape the library's calculated position.
beats.heading: The CSS rule that fights the library

notes: The mechanism by which absolute positioning on a child of a Radix portal undermines collision detection is inferred from how Radix computes placement (via transform on the portal root) — a child with its own absolute offset then moves relative to its nearest positioned ancestor, which may not be the portal root.

steps.headline: The boundary guard was there but bypassed
steps.narration: The floating panel library already had a collision boundary set to the editor container, which should have prevented overflow. But an absolute positioning rule on the inner wrapper let it move independently from where the library placed the outer shell. So the fix requires touching both the side selection and the stylesheet.
steps.routeLabel: Why Radix can't fix it alone

steps.say: Instead of just removing the absolute-positioning rule, the inner wrapper div is removed entirely and the picker's visual class moves onto the floating panel element itself.

lines.annotation: Extra wrapper div carrying the `.picker` class — and via CSS, `position: absolute`.

beats.text: Before the change, the library's popover root was a bare container, and a nested `<div>` inside it carried all the visual styles.
beats.heading: The old structure

lines.annotation: The class now belongs to the Radix-positioned element, so there is no extra positioned child to escape.
`alignOffset` nudges the popup 12 px along the alignment axis, replacing the gap that the inner div's margin previously provided.

beats.text: The `className`, `role`, `aria-modal`, and `aria-label` attributes move up onto `Popover.Content`; the wrapper `<div>` is removed. The `.picker` CSS rule loses `position: absolute`.
beats.heading: What we change

steps.title: Flatten the wrapper div; let Radix own the visual box
steps.headline: Promote the picker styles onto the Radix element directly
steps.narration: Simply removing the absolute-positioning rule from the stylesheet would have been the smallest change. But the inner wrapper was also the element carrying the popup's visual appearance — its background, shadow, and rounded corners. The right move is to remove the extra wrapper entirely and put the styling directly on the element the library positions. That way the library controls the one positioned root, and the visual appearance travels with it.

summary.problem: The arrowhead picker popup could overflow the viewport edge because it was positioned with `position: absolute` in CSS (which let it escape its Radix boundary) and, on phones, was sent to `side='right'` where the panel is near the right edge of the screen.
summary.solution: Remove `position: absolute` from the picker's CSS so Radix controls placement entirely, lock the side to `bottom`, add `alignOffset` to keep it away from the edge, and flatten the extra wrapper div so the Radix content element itself carries the picker's visual styling.
